topics.name: Present and past perfect continuous with since / for

options: If the parrot will be ill, we will take it to the vet.
If the parrot is ill, we will take it to the vet.
If the parrot is ill, we took it to the vet.
questions.rule: Type 1: If + simple present, will + base verb. No 'will' in the if-part.

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct tense.
options: The puppy has been sleeping for morning.
The puppy has been sleeping since morning.
The puppy have been sleeping since morning.
questions.rule: since + starting point (morning). The puppy is singular, so has been.

questions.rule: for + a length of time (ten years); since + a starting point (2015).

questions.before: The vet asked me if my cat
questions.rule: Reported yes/no question: if + subject + verb in the past: if my cat was drinking.
Modal passive: modal + be + past participle: must be kept.
If + simple present, will + base verb: If you feed the cat, it will purr.

chat: Why are your eyes so red?
options: I have been reading since lunch.
I have been read since lunch.
questions.rule: An action from a past point until now: have been reading since lunch.

questions.source: Asha asked me, "Do you have a pet?"
options: Asha asked me if I had a pet.
Asha asked me if you had a pet.
Asha asked me do I have a pet.
questions.rule: Yes/no question: use if, change you to I, and have to had.

questions.source: We should feed the birds every day.
options: The birds should be feed every day.
The birds should be fed every day.
The birds should fed every day.
questions.rule: should + be + past participle: should be fed.

options: The keeper asked why was the lion not eating.
The keeper asked why the lion is not eat.
The keeper asked why the lion was not eating.
questions.rule: In a reported question, the subject comes before the verb: why the lion was not eating.

options: The horse's leg must checked by a vet.
The horse's leg must be check by a vet.
The horse's leg must be checked by a vet.
questions.rule: must + be + past participle: must be checked.

questions.rule: Present perfect continuous: has (not) been + -ing: has not been singing.

questions.after: a cold, it will stay in its shelter.
questions.rule: Type 1: the if-part takes the simple present (catches); the result takes will.

questions.after: I wanted to become a vet.
questions.rule: A reported yes/no question uses whether or if, not 'that'.
Subject + must be + past participle: The injection must be given today.

options: If he doesn't eat by evening, we'll take him to the vet.
If he don't eat by evening, we'll take him to the vet.
If he doesn't eat by evening, we took him to the vet.

chat: How long has your dog been limping?
options: He has been limping since Monday.
He has been limp since Monday.
questions.rule: Answer in the same tense: has been limping since Monday.

questions.source: If you do not clean the cage, the birds will fall ill.
options: Unless you do not clean the cage, the birds will fall ill.
Unless you clean the cage, the birds will fall ill.
Unless you clean the cage, the birds would fall ill.
questions.rule: unless = if not, so drop the 'not': Unless you clean the cage... Keep will.

questions.rule: had (not) + past participle: had not eaten. Modal passive: must be given.

options: If I were a vet, I would treat lions and tigers.
If I were a vet, I would treated lions and tigers.
If I were a vet, I will treat lions and tigers.

chat: Help! The elephant has swallowed a paper bag!
options: The vet must be call at once!
The vet must been called at once!
The vet must be called at once!

chat: What did the vet ask you?
options: He asked me how often did I feed the dog.
He asked me how often I fed the dog.
He asked me how often I feed to the dog.
questions.rule: Reported question: no 'did', statement order, past tense: how often I fed the dog.

questions.prompt: Join into one sentence using the present perfect continuous.
questions.source: Arjun started training as a vet in 2022. He is still training.
options: Arjun has been training as a vet for 2022.
Arjun has been training as a vet since 2022.
Arjun is training as a vet since 2022.
questions.rule: Started in the past and still going on: has been training since 2022.

questions.source: If the monkey stops pinching its tail, it will feel better.
options: If the monkey stopped pinching its tail, it will feel better.
If the monkey stopped pinching its tail, it would feel better.
If the monkey stops pinching its tail, it would feel better.
questions.rule: Type 2: If + simple past (stopped), would + base verb.

questions.rule: will + base verb (feel). Type 2 if-part takes the past: if they had more space.

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct tense.
options: We have been visiting this zoo since we were children.
We are visiting this zoo since we were children.
We have been visiting this zoo since we are children.
questions.rule: Main clause: present perfect continuous. After since, the past: since we were children.

chat: Can I give my puppy some chocolate?
options: No! Chocolate should never be given to dogs.
No! Chocolate should never be give to dogs.
No! Chocolate should never given to dogs.

questions.source: The vet said to the keeper, "Has the bear eaten its buns?"
options: The vet asked the keeper had the bear eaten its buns.
The vet asked the keeper if the bear had eaten its buns.
The vet asked the keeper if the bear had ate its buns.
questions.rule: said to → asked, add if, statement order, has eaten → had eaten.

questions.source: The zookeeper must give the hippo its medicine.

The hippo must given its medicine by the zookeeper.
The hippo must be given its medicine by the zookeeper.
